title: A recipe is a versioned file: identity, resolution, launch
design_ref: A recipe is a pipeline of stages; The experiment platform on Kubernetes
purpose: One YAML file fully describes a run. Its identity is the hash of its content, not of its formatting. Launching it pins every reference (data, model, image, code, Git commit) in the tracking store before a pod exists, and labels the job with the hash.

checks.because: The hash is sha256 of the parsed recipe serialised as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace), so comments, key order and indentation do not count.

checks.description: one changed value gives a different identity
checks.because: Any change to what the run does changes the canonical JSON.

checks.description: every reference is pinned: datasets by content hash, the base model by commit, the image by digest
checks.because: The launcher looks each dataset up in the index and copies its hash, refuses a Hugging Face model without a full commit, and uses the image digest.

checks.description: the run's resolved description is in the tracking store, from a committed recipe, with the hash of the code the cluster runs
checks.because: The launcher writes runs/<id>/resolved.json before it creates the Job, and refuses to launch if the cluster's code ConfigMap differs from the checkout.

checks.description: the Job carries the recipe hash and the production queue
checks.because: The launcher sets the labels; Kueue reads the queue label.

checks.description: Kueue admitted it through the production queue at production priority
checks.because: The queue label made Kueue create a Workload; the priority-class label gave it the production class's value, 1000.

checks.description: the description existed before the pod did
checks.because: The launcher writes to S3 first and only then calls the API server.
